title: Consolidated generation surface: PRD and launch checklist for unified hosted endpoints
creator: Aisha Patel
overview: This PRD defines the scope, requirements, acceptance criteria, and launch checklist for a consolidated generation surface in the hosted API that harmonizes chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank endpoints into a lightweight, consistent developer experience. The goal is to reduce cognitive overhead for integrators, provide consistent behavioral contracts (streaming, structured output, errors), and make the first-phase launch safe for production customers with clear rollback and monitoring paths.
goals: 1) Ship a single, well-documented surface for text generation primitives that supports chat-style stateful streams and stateless completions. 2) Expose embeddings and rerank as consistent companion endpoints with shared auth, quotas, and telemetry. 3) Meet target SLOs (95th pct latency targets and error budgets) for GA customers. 4) Provide migration guides and SDK updates so existing integrations can switch with minimal changes.
non_goals: 1) Not migrating legacy dedicated or private deployments in this phase. 2) Not changing billing model beyond mapping to existing usage meters. 3) Not supporting all existing experimental model flags — advanced optimization knobs will be a follow-up.
scope_changes: Initial scoping included multi-region simultaneous GA and an aggressive SDK surface parity. After engineering capacity review (2026-02-28) scope was reduced: region rollout will be staged (US then EU) and SDK language parity will be limited to JS and Python for GA. Function-calling shim will be deferred to next release. These scope changes were approved by PM and Eng leads on 2026-03-03.
requirements: Functional requirements: 1) Single authentication and tenant routing for all four endpoint types. 2) Predictable streaming behavior for chat (chunk framing, token boundaries, partial delta semantics). 3) Deterministic structured output support (JSON schema enforcement option). 4) Embeddings endpoint returns vector floats with stable dimensionality per model and includes model metadata. 5) Rerank accepts candidate lists and returns score+rank with reproducible tie-handling. Non-functional requirements: 1) 95th percentile latency targets: completions < 180ms for <512 tokens, chat streaming first-byte < 120ms. 2) Error rate < 0.2% for core happy-paths. 3) Full tracing spans emitted and accessible in Console. 4) Per-route cost breakdowns available in billing exports.
api_surface: Design principle: keep simple default paths, allow opt-in advanced flags. Endpoint roadmap: POST /v1/generate (unified surface) supports type parameter {chat|completion} and streaming via SSE/websocket; POST /v1/embeddings returns vectors and model metadata; POST /v1/rerank accepts {query, candidates[]} and returns ordered indices with scores. Backwards compatibility: existing /v1/chat-completions and /v1/embeddings endpoints will be route aliases for 6 months with deprecation warnings. OpenAPI spec link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/specs/unified-generation-openapi (draft). SDK changes: JS and Python clients add GenerateClient.generate(...) convenience helper and embeddings/rerank wrappers. Rate limits: per-tenant token-based quotas with soft-burst policy defined in billing playbook.
acceptance_criteria: 1) API contract verified by integration tests covering chat streaming, completion sync, embeddings shape, and rerank determinism. 2) Load test: sustained 2k RPS across generation endpoints with P95 latency within targets on the provisioned GA cluster. 3) Canary rollout (1% traffic) for 48 hours with error rate and latency within thresholds and no customer-visible anomalies. 4) SDKs published (JS/Python) with changelog, migration guide, and two example apps updated in the repo. 5) Console dashboards show per-route token cost, tail latency, error rates, and a rollout toggle to force fallback. 6) Security review completed and signed-off; KMS integration exercised for private key materials used in telemetry. 7) Billing mapping validated with finance: per-token metrics populate billing exports and invoice preview matches sample customers.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal beta — invite-only access with sample customers and partners for 2 weeks. Phase 1: Canary 1% traffic US-only for 48 hours (monitoring gates). Phase 2: Ramp to 10% over 72 hours if gates pass. Phase 3: EU region canary for 48 hours, then global GA. Rollback: automatic fallback policy to previous endpoint alias if error rate exceeds 0.5% or P95 latency regresses by >40% for 10-minute window. Communication: release notes, console banner for tenants, and customer success outreach for top 50 customers.
launch_checklist: Pre-launch: 1) Merge API gateway routing PR (GH: redwood/api#1287). 2) SDK releases published and NPM/PyPI packages available with pre-release tags. 3) OpenAPI and migration docs live in Confluence and /docs. 4) Add deprecation header to alias endpoints. 5) Run chaos test plan (simulate transient GPU OOM) and verify fallback. 6) Security review and pen-test findings closed. Launch day: 1) Enable canary via feature flag (FF: gen_unified_canary). 2) Run smoke test suite against canary traffic. 3) Monitor dashboards and alert channels (pager on-call if thresholds hit). 4) Notify customers via status page that canary is live. Post-launch: 1) Ramp per rollout plan. 2) Collect SDK crash reports and telemetry for first 72 hours. 3) Open post-mortem channel for incidents and track to closure within 7 days.
monitoring_and_slo: Dashboards required: per-endpoint latency histogram, error-rate (4xx/5xx) split, token consumption, per-customer tail latency. Alerts: page if 5-minute error rate > 0.5% or P95 latency exceeds target by 30% for 10 minutes. SLOs: 99.5% availability per month; latency SLOs as defined in requirements. Cost monitoring: per-route unit cost visible in Console with anomaly detection for sudden token spikes.
dependencies: Engineering: runtime batching and KV caching improvements (ENG-23812), gateway feature-flagging infra (ENG-26111). SDK: JS/Python client owners. Security: KMS and audit logging sign-off. Finance: billing export schema change (PM-52673). Legal: terms update if embeddings routing changes. Customer success: migration outreach for top accounts.
risks_mitigation: Risk: Streaming semantics incompatibility with some customers. Mitigation: provide 'compatibility_mode' flag that emulates legacy chunk framing. Risk: Burst traffic blowup causing latency spikes. Mitigation: soft-burst circuit-breakers and autoscaling rules with conservative initial thresholds. Risk: Billing misattribution. Mitigation: validate sample invoices and hold GA until finance sign-off.
docs_and_training: Deliverables: migration guide (step-by-step from legacy endpoints), SDK code samples for chat and completions, embeddings best-practices doc, rerank scoring FAQ, runbook for on-call, and customer-facing changelog. Training: 2 internal office hours with developer advocates, updated CS playbook with troubleshooting checklist.
open_questions: 1) Final decision on alias deprecation period: 3 months vs 6 months? Target decision date 2026-03-20. 2) Should function-calling be shimmed for GA or deferred? Engineering recommends deferral. 3) Do we require explicit consent for reranking candidate storage in analytics? Legal to advise by 2026-03-18.
